node.label: Paul Ricœur
node.date_label: 1983: Temps et récit I · 1984: Temps et récit II: La configuration dans le récit de fiction · 1985: Temps et récit III: Le temps raconté · 2000: La mémoire, l’histoire et l’oubli
node.description: A philosopher of interpretation, narrative and historical knowledge. He distinguishes memory’s recognition from history’s documentary criticism, and treats shifts of historical scale as a resource for examining determination and uncertainty.
node.representative_figures_and_works: Temps et récit I (1983); Temps et récit II: La configuration dans le récit de fiction (1984); Temps et récit III: Le temps raconté (1985); La mémoire, l’histoire et l’oubli (2000).

proposed_edges.relationship: Distinguishes recollective recognition from the critical comparison of testimonies and documents in historical knowledge.
proposed_edges.evidence_note: Own dialogue, PDF pp. 4–5, passage from recognition to the archive; testimony is fallible and can be criticized. Personal forgiveness is explicitly distinguished from state amnesty and judicial impunity in PDF pp. 1–3. Book body unread.

proposed_edges.relationship: Uses movement between historical scales to think about determination, uncertainty and actors’ limited horizons.
proposed_edges.evidence_note: Own dialogue, PDF pp. 5–7, discussions of Revel, Braudel and Menocchio. This is an epistemological resource attributed to Ricoeur, not a claim that he practised or founded microhistory, or independent verification of his account of other historians.
